    Automatic exploratory data analysis¶

    Use tsdst.eda to explore a dataset without a response variable. This module builds on the type rules, correlation checks, and plots in the Kaggle Common_Data_Science_Functions.py file. It adds data summaries, checks for common data issues, and an HTML report.

    Get started¶

    import pandas as pd
from tsdst.eda import auto_eda

data = pd.read_csv("my_data.csv")
report = auto_eda(data, output_file="reports/eda.html")

report.overview             # Check row counts, missing values, and duplicates.
report.variables            # Review types, counts, and summary statistics.
report.frequencies          # Get full category counts, including missing values.
report.correlations         # Review numeric correlations.
report.high_correlations    # Get each pair that meets the threshold.
report.alerts               # Check data issues that need review.

# Save another copy of the report.
report.to_file("reports/another_copy.html")

    Display report in a notebook to view the tables and plots. Each HTML report includes its styles and plot images. You can open the report without an internet connection.

    If you omit the output path, the function returns the report without writing a file. The analysis keeps the input unchanged. It does not fit a model, fill missing values, or remove features.

    Types and statistics¶

    The module treats strings, categories, and booleans as categorical variables. Datetime and timedelta columns receive date summaries. A numeric column with at most five unique nonmissing values is also categorical. This rule follows the starter code. Use n_unique=None to disable it.

    To set a type for a specific column, use feature_types:

    report = auto_eda(
    data,
    feature_types={"account_id": "categorical", "rating": "numeric"},
    corr_method="spearman",
    corr_threshold=0.8,
)

    A type override does not convert the data. If a string represents a date or number, convert it in pandas before you run the analysis. Each cell must contain one scalar, hashable value. Each column must have a unique label. The module does not support complex numbers.

    Missing fractions use the full row or cell count. Unique counts exclude missing values. Unique fractions use the count of nonmissing values. Numeric statistics exclude missing and infinite values. The report counts infinities separately and uses sample standard deviation.

    The outlier count uses the interquartile range (IQR). It counts values below the first quartile minus 1.5 times the IQR. It also counts values above the third quartile plus 1.5 times the IQR.

    Correlations use numeric features only. Each pair uses rows with valid values for both features. Each pair that meets the absolute threshold appears once and keeps its correlation sign. Use corr_threshold=None to skip correlations.

    Use the alerts to review the data. Constants, unique values, strong correlations, and outliers can be useful. The alerts do not remove features.

    Compare an optional response¶

    If you have a response variable, supply its column name, a separate Series, or a one-dimensional array. A Series must have the same index as the features. An array must have one value per row.

    report = auto_eda(data, response="outcome", response_type="categorical")

    If you supply a column name, the module excludes that column from the feature summaries. The response receives a separate profile.

    Plot types depend on the two variables:

    • Two categorical variables use grouped bar plots.

    • One numeric and one categorical variable use box plots.

    • Two numeric variables use scatter plots.

    Numeric responses also receive feature correlations. Date variables have distribution plots. Response comparison plots skip date variables. These comparisons do not fit models or select features.

    Control work and output¶

    # Compute tables without plots.
report = auto_eda(data, plots=False)

# Add a scatter matrix with row and column limits.
report = auto_eda(
    data,
    plot_pairs=True,
    max_pair_columns=8,
    max_plot_rows=5000,
    max_categories=20,
    random_state=42,
)

    Statistics and category counts use the full dataset. Only response plots and scatter matrices can use a row sample. The scatter matrix selects numeric columns in input order, up to the column limit.

    Correlations use all numeric features. Their computation cost grows with the square of the number of numeric features.

    Category distribution bars combine values beyond the display limit. Grouped response plots show the most frequent categories only. Full category counts remain available in report.frequencies. The report records plot limits and row sampling in report.notes and the HTML.

    API¶

    tsdst.eda.auto_eda(features, response=None, *, title='Exploratory data analysis', n_unique=5, feature_types=None, response_type=None, corr_threshold=0.3, corr_method='pearson', plots=True, plot_pairs=False, max_categories=20, max_plot_rows=5000, max_pair_columns=8, random_state=0, output_file=None)[source]

    Explore tabular data and return an EDA report.

    Parameters:
    featurespandas.DataFrame or two-dimensional array-like

    Data to explore. Each column must have a unique label. Each cell must contain one scalar, hashable value. The analysis keeps the input unchanged.

    responsestr, pandas.Series, or one-dimensional array-like, optional

    A column name or a separate response. If you supply a column name, exclude that column from the features. A Series must have the same index as the features. Arrays match by row position. The response is optional. This function does not fit a model.

    titlestr

    Report title.

    n_uniqueint or None

    Treat numeric columns as categorical if their unique count is at most this value. Exclude missing values from the count. Set None to disable this rule. Booleans are categorical.

    feature_typesdict, optional

    Set a column type to ‘numeric’, ‘categorical’, or ‘date’. Numeric and date types require a compatible dtype. Convert strings to numbers or dates before you call this function.

    response_typestr, optional

    Set the response type with the same rules as feature_types.

    corr_thresholdfloat or None

    Absolute threshold from 0 to 1, inclusive. Set None to skip correlations. Use numeric features only. Exclude infinite values.

    corr_method{‘pearson’, ‘spearman’, ‘kendall’}

    Correlation method. Each pair uses rows with valid values for both variables.

    plotsbool

    Create plots for distributions, missing values, and correlations. If you supply a response, add comparison plots. Set False to compute tables only.

    plot_pairsbool

    Include a scatter matrix for numeric features. Set plots=True to use this option.

    max_categoriesint

    Maximum number of categories to show. Distribution bars combine the other categories. Response comparisons show the most frequent categories only.

    max_plot_rowsint or None

    Row limit for scatter matrices and response comparisons. Statistics, frequencies, and distribution plots use all rows. Set None to use all rows in every plot. Use random_state to repeat the same row sample.

    max_pair_columnsint

    Maximum number of numeric columns in the scatter matrix. Select columns in input order. Correlations use all numeric features.

    random_stateint

    Seed for the row sample in the plots.

    output_filestr or pathlib.Path, optional

    Path for the HTML report. If you omit this path, return the report without writing a file.

    Returns:
    EDAReport

    Summary tables, alerts, and plots. Export the report to HTML or display it in a notebook.

    class tsdst.eda.EDAReport(title, overview, variables, frequencies, correlations, high_correlations, alerts, plots, response_summary, response_correlations, notes, max_categories)[source]

    Store the tables and PNG plots from auto_eda().

    Attributes:
    overviewdict

    Row and column counts, missing values, duplicate rows, and memory use.

    variablespandas.DataFrame

    One row per feature. Numeric statistics use finite values only. Missing values and infinities have separate counts. Missing fractions use the full row count. Unique counts exclude missing values. Unique fractions use the count of nonmissing values.

    frequenciesdict

    Full value counts for categorical features, including missing values.

    correlationspandas.DataFrame

    Correlations between numeric features. Each pair uses rows with valid values for both features.

    high_correlationspandas.DataFrame

    One row per pair that meets the absolute threshold. Correlations keep their signs.

    alertspandas.DataFrame

    Checks for missing values, constants, unique values, infinities, duplicate rows, and correlated features. Use these checks to review the data. The checks do not remove features.

    plotsdict

    PNG images encoded as base64 text. Keys are (section, variable) tuples.

    response_summarypandas.Series or None

    A separate profile of the optional response.

    response_correlationspandas.Series or None

    Correlations with numeric features, if the response is numeric.

    noteslist of str

    Row sampling and limits on the plots.

    to_file(path)[source]

    Write an HTML report and return its path.

    to_html(path=None)[source]

    Return an HTML report with its styles and plot images.

    If you supply a path, write the report as a UTF-8 file. Create missing parent directories. Replace an existing file at that path. Escape dataset labels and values for HTML.
